correctness.rationale: Normalized-area monomial orthogonality changes only the m-th diagonal coefficient; exact expansion gives 1/(1-t)^2-c t^m with 0<=c<m+1. All boundary roots are obtained by the phase identity t^m(1-t)^2=4sin^2(theta/2)e^{i((m+1)theta+pi)}; every boundary crossing enters inward because Re[m-2t/(1-t)]=m+1>0 there. An interior multiple root cannot occur at allowed c, since c*4m^m/(m+2)^(m+2)<4(m+1)/(m+2)^2<1. Rouché starts the count at zero. Strict monotonicity of 4n sin^2(pi/(2n)) and F(9)>1>F(10) prove order-eight/nine threshold, and odd-angle counting with c_n~n proves N=n-sqrt(n)/pi+O(1) for fixed positive penalty. checks.py executed and printed VERIFY_OK 1130 finite assertions; finite data are not used to prove any infinite statement.

value.rationale: The space is a natural positive Sobolev rank-one regularization of classical Bergman evaluation geometry. Exact jet-by-penalty Lu Qi-Keng zero-fibre thresholds go beyond the trivial kernel subtraction, and exhibit a nontrivial universal barrier exactly at derivative order nine. The fixed-penalty sqrt(m) missing-root law reveals an asymptotic constraint relevant to high-order jet regularization. The claimed invariant is naturally the number of zero fibres because any such fibre represents infinitely many pairs (z,w).
